- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.3) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid missing reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for sudden sentiment reversal and adjust forecast mid-series (e.g., +2–4% in 3–5 days).
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 60–70% of forecast range); add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment is bullish in last 3–5 days, add 1–2% to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid “bottoming too early.”
